title: Arrows with size and direction
objectives: Represent a displacement as a column vector.
Find the vector between two points as end minus start.

screens.title: Arrows with size and direction
screens.prose: A move on a map has a size and a direction. We will record any move as two numbers, then reason with the numbers.
A counter slides along the arrow, from A at $(1, 1)$ to B at $(4, 3)$. Each grid square is one unit.

state.caption: A is at (1, 1) and B is at (4, 3)

screens.question: How far across and how far up does the counter move?

options.why: You read off where the head is. The slide starts at (1, 1), so count from there.
You swapped the two moves. Across runs from 1 to 4, which is 3.
That is how far it goes, but not which way. Two numbers are needed to fix the direction.

hints.text: Start counting at the tail of the arrow, not at the origin.
Follow the arrow from (1, 1) to (4, 3).
Across: from 1 to 4 is 3. Up: from 1 to 3 is 2.

feedback.correct: 3 across and 2 up, counted from the tail.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count the squares from the tail of the arrow to its head.

byKey.head: You read off where the head is. The slide starts at (1, 1), so count from there.

explain.text: You counted from the tail at $(1, 1)$ to the head at $(4, 3)$: 3 across, then 2 up. Those two numbers fix the move completely. The two extra arrows show them.

screens.prose: Drag the head of the arrow anywhere on the grid. The caption reads the move as across and up. Try every corner.
screens.question: A move goes 2 left and 3 down. Which pair of signed numbers records it, across first?

options.why: You dropped the signs. $(2, 3)$ is 2 right and 3 up.
You put the up-down number first. Across always comes first.
Left is the negative direction across, so the first number is $-2$.

feedback.correct: Left and down are the negative directions.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Drag the head 2 left and 3 down, then read the caption.

explain.text: Right and up count as positive, left and down as negative. So 2 left and 3 down is $(-2, -3)$. The sign gives the direction and the size gives the distance.

screens.prose: A move written as two signed numbers is a **vector**. We stack them in a column, across on top: $\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$ is 3 right and 1 up. The two numbers are its **components**.
screens.question: Drag the head of the arrow so that $\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$.

hints.text: The top number is the move across. Which way is negative across?
The head must end up left of the vertical axis and above the horizontal one.
From the origin go 3 squares left, then 2 squares up.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The top component moves the head across, the bottom one moves it up.

byKey.swapped: Your head sits at $(2, -3)$: you used the bottom number for across. The top number is always across.
byKey.sign-top: Your arrow points right. The top component is $-3$, so the head goes 3 left.
byKey.sign-bottom: Your arrow points down. The bottom component is $+2$, so the head goes 2 up.
byKey.v: Not there yet. From the origin go 3 left and 2 up.

explain.text: The top component, $-3$, sends the head 3 left. The bottom component, $2$, lifts it 2 up. Every arrow from the origin is one column vector, and every column vector is one arrow.

screens.prose: Four more arrows are drawn in different places. The first one, $\mathbf{u}$, starts at the origin.
screens.question: Which arrows are the same vector as $\mathbf{u}$? Select all that apply.

options.why: B is as long as $\mathbf{u}$ but points the other way. It is $(-2, -1)$.
C swaps the components: 1 across and 2 up.

hints.text: For each arrow, count across and up from its tail to its head.
Check which way B points: its head is on the left.
$\mathbf{u}$ is $(2, 1)$. A and D also go 2 right and 1 up. B goes 2 left and 1 down.

feedback.correct: A and D make the same move as u from different starting points.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the moves, not the positions.

byKey.B: You picked B, which points the other way: 2 left and 1 down.
byKey.Cc: You picked C, which goes 1 across and 2 up. The components are swapped.

explain.text: A and D each go 2 right and 1 up, the same move as $\mathbf{u}$. A vector records only the move, so where we draw it does not change it. B reverses the move and C swaps its components.

screens.prose: A drone flies straight from $A(1, 4)$ to $B(6, 1)$. We write the vector from A to B as $\overrightarrow{AB}$.

state.caption: A is at (1, 4) and B is at (6, 1)

screens.question: Fill in the two components of $\overrightarrow{AB}$.

hints.text: For each component, take where the drone ends minus where it starts.
The drone drops from a height of 4 to a height of 1.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take the end coordinate minus the start coordinate in each row.

byKey.r0c1: Check the across component. It runs from 1 to 6: subtract the start from the end.
byKey.r1c1: Check the up component. The drone falls from 4 to 1, so the component is negative.

explain.text: Across: $6 - 1 = 5$. Up: $1 - 4 = -3$, negative because the drone drops. So $\overrightarrow{AB} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix}$: end minus start in each row.

screens.prose: Two points: $P(4, 3)$ and $Q(1, 5)$. The arrows $\mathbf{p}$ and $\mathbf{q}$ run from the origin to each point. A ball rolls from P to Q.
screens.question: Which vector is $\overrightarrow{PQ}$, the move of the ball?

options.why: You took start minus end. That is the move from Q back to P.
That is where Q sits, measured from the origin. The ball starts at P, not at the origin.
You added the two positions. A move is the difference between them.

hints.text: The ball starts at P. Where does it end?
Compare the heads of the two arrows.

feedback.correct: 3 left and 2 up, from P to Q.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take where the ball ends minus where it starts.

byKey.back: You took start minus end, $P - Q$. That is the reverse trip, from Q to P.
byKey.end: You gave the position of Q. A move from P has to start at P.

explain.text: $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ runs from the head of $\mathbf{p}$ to the head of $\mathbf{q}$: end minus start gives $\begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$. Start minus end gives the reverse trip. The coordinates of Q alone describe a trip from the origin.

screens.prose: You took end minus start in each row. Now do it for any two points, $A(a_1, a_2)$ and $B(b_1, b_2)$.
screens.question: Which column vector is $\overrightarrow{AB}$?

options.why: You took start minus end. That gives the move from B back to A.
That is where B sits, seen from the origin. The move starts at A.
You mixed the rows. Across uses the first coordinates only, up the second.

hints.text: Which point does the move start at, and which does it end at?
Each row is the end coordinate minus the start coordinate, in the same row.
Top row: $b_1 - a_1$. Bottom row: $b_2 - a_2$.

feedback.correct: End minus start, row by row.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Put end minus start in each row, across on top.

byKey.back: You took start minus end. That gives the move from B back to A.

explain.text: So $\overrightarrow{AB} = \begin{pmatrix} b_1 - a_1 \\ b_2 - a_2 \end{pmatrix} = \mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a}$. Here $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are the **position vectors** of A and B, the arrows from the origin. End minus start, always.

screens.prose: A fund holds 300 shares of Alpha and 200 of Beta. After a rebalance it holds 150 of Alpha and 450 of Beta. Each holding is a vector, in hundreds of shares on the diagram.
screens.question: What trade vector takes the old holdings to the new ones? Give numbers of shares.

hints.text: The trade is the move from the old holdings to the new ones.
Which arrow on the diagram is the trade? Where does it start?
Trade = after minus before: $150 - 300$ for Alpha, $450 - 200$ for Beta.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take the holdings after minus the holdings before, stock by stock.

byKey.r0c1: Check Alpha. The fund goes from 300 down to 150 shares, so the trade is negative: a sale.
byKey.r1c1: Check Beta. It goes from 200 to 450 shares: after minus before.

explain.text: $\text{after} - \text{before} = \begin{pmatrix} 150 \\ 450 \end{pmatrix} - \begin{pmatrix} 300 \\ 200 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -150 \\ 250 \end{pmatrix}$. The minus sign means sell 150 Alpha. The holdings are position vectors and the trade is the move between them.

ideas: A vector records a move: how far across and how far up, with signs for the direction.
Arrows that make the same move are the same vector, wherever they are drawn.
The vector from A to B is end minus start: $\overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a}$.

formula.name: Vector between two points
formula.note: Start minus end gives $\overrightarrow{BA}$, the reverse move.

summary.trap: The vector from P to Q is neither the coordinates of Q nor P minus Q. Take end minus start.

quiz.prose: A ship sails in a straight line from $(-2, 3)$ to $(4, -1)$.
quiz.question: Which column vector is the ship's move?

options.why: You took start minus end. That is the trip back.
That is where the ship ends, not how far it moved.
You added the two points. A move is a difference.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take end minus start in each row.

explain.text: Across: $4 - (-2) = 6$. Up: $-1 - 3 = -4$. So the move is $\begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}$.

quiz.prose: A courier drives from depot D to a shop S, then straight back to D.
quiz.question: Which vector is the courier's total move?

options.why: You doubled the outward trip. The trip back undoes it.
That is the outward trip only. The way back cancels it.
That is the way back only. The outward trip cancels it.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Where does the courier end, compared with where they started?

explain.text: The courier ends where they started, so the total move is end minus start: zero in both rows. This is the **zero vector**, $\mathbf{0}$. It is the one vector with no direction.

quiz.prose: The vector $\mathbf{w}$ moves 4 left and 1 up.
quiz.question: Which column vector is $\mathbf{w}$?

options.why: You put the up move on top. Across goes on top.
You dropped the sign. Left is negative.
You swapped the rows and moved the sign.

feedback.correct: Across on top, with left negative.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Across goes on top, and left counts as negative.

explain.text: Across on top: 4 left is $-4$. Up below: 1 up is $1$. So $\mathbf{w} = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$.

quiz.prose: ABCD is a parallelogram, with its corners labelled in order around the shape.
quiz.question: Which vector equals $\overrightarrow{AB}$?

options.why: CD is the opposite side, but traced the other way, from C to D.
BC is the next side round. It points in a different direction.
AC is a diagonal. It is longer and points another way.

feedback.correct: Opposite sides of a parallelogram make the same move.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the side that makes the same move as A to B.

explain.text: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel and equal in length. Going from D to C makes the same move as going from A to B. So $\overrightarrow{DC} = \overrightarrow{AB}$, while $\overrightarrow{CD} = -\overrightarrow{AB}$.
